items.rationale: The shed is an insured site installation (4.2.5) damaged by a storm-thrown tree (2.5.3(c)). Disposal of the remains of insured property is covered under 5.2.1(a) and 7.1.7(a); a moderate disposal fee for a shed-roof load applies.

items.description: Disposal of broken shed glass pane
items.rationale: Glazing is a building component of the shed (4.2.2), so its remains are material arising under 5.2.1(a). This is a small disposal charge.

items.description: Disposal of green waste from felled tree
items.rationale: Vegetation the storm felled onto the insured site counts as material arising under 5.2.1(b) and 2.5.3(c), even though the tree itself is uninsured (4.3(e)). A moderate green-waste disposal fee applies.

items.description: Disposal of root ball under 1 m³
items.rationale: A single root mass not exceeding one cubic metre is expressly material arising under 5.2.1(b). The description confirms it was under 1 m³, so it falls under the clearance head rather than 5.2.2.

Topsoil is ground material, which is excluded from clearance under 5.2.1(d) and uninsured under 4.3(d). There is no reinstatement with making good of the ground, so 5.2.2 fails and the standalone disposal is not indemnified: t = 0.
Paving grit is defined as ground material (1.3) and is excluded under 5.2.1(d). This is a standalone disposal with no making good under 5.2.2(c), so t = 0.
Excavated soil is ground material, excluded under 5.2.1(d). 5.2.2 expressly bars disposal of ground material as a standalone clearance measure, so t = 0.
